newsitem.title: HONG KONG: HK graft probe into U.S. immigration takes twist.
newsitem.headline: HK graft probe into U.S. immigration takes twist.

text.p: A probe into a senior United States immigration officer in Hong Kong took a new twist on Tuesday when the territory's corruption watchdog said it had hauled in his jailed former colleague for questioning.
The move came as the Independent Commission Against Corruption (ICAC) and U.S. investigators conducted an inquiry into James DeBates, head of immigration at the U.S. Consulate in this British colony.
The ICAC told Reuters that Jerry Stuchiner, a former senior officer of the U.S. Immigration and Naturalisation Service, had been transferred to its custody from a Hong Kong prison.
"He is in ICAC custody to assist in corruption investigations," a spokesman for the commission said.
The commission refused to give further details and would not be drawn on whether the move was linked to the DeBates case.
Stuchiner, who was once DeBates' superior, was jailed for 40 months last August after being caught with fake Honduran passports believed to be linked to an immigrant smuggling ring.
DeBates has been sent back to the United States on "administrative leave" while the latest investigation continues.
U.S. Consul-General Richard Boucher has vowed to root out corruption from his mission, the largest U.S. consulate in the world.
The case comes amid concern that hundreds of illegals, many of them from China, may have entered the United States on documents obtained through the consulate in Hong Kong.
